TINGCUNGCO City Council Secretary Sangguniang Panlungsod ng Marikina Dear Ms. Tingcungco: This has reference to the letter received by this Department last 2 May 2024 pertaining to the request for legal advice and guidance on the proposed ordinance of Marikina. The subject document is titled, "Proposed Ordinance Separating the Building and Grounds Management Division (BGMD) from the General Services Office (GSO) and its Establishment as an Independent Office, Creating Various Plantilla Positions and Appropriating Funds Thereof You wish to be clarified on the following points, to wit: (1) Is the enactment of the proposed ordinance within the authority of the city council, as outlined in RA 7160, or is it considered ultra vires? (2) Is it possible to legally separate the BGMD as a Division from its main office at GSO without negatively affecting its mandate and service? (3) Would such a separation comply with all rules and regulations set forth by the Civil Service Commission? In essence, the issue hinges on the validity and legality of the subject proposed ordinance. With regard to the first issue, the Department had on one occasion the opportunity to rule on similar facts and circumstances. We cite the salient portions applicable to the case and attach a copy of the Department's Legal Opinion No. 43, s. 2020 for your ready reference, to wit. Foremost, local govemment units (LGUs), like the Sangguniang Panlungsod, of Malaybalay, Bukidnon are vested by the Local Govemment Code the power to legislate for the general welfare of their constituents. Section 458 (a) of the Code provides, viz: "The sangguniang panlungsod, as the legislative body of the city, shall enact ordinances, approve resolutions and appropriate funds for the general welfare of the city and its inhabitants pursuant to Sec. 16 of this Code and in the proper exercise of the corporate powers of the city as provided for under Section 22 of this Code xxx" Section 16 of the Code provides that: "Matino. "Every local govemment unit shall exercise the powers expressly granted, those necessarily implied therefrom, as well as powers necessary, appropriate, or incidental for its efficient and effective govemance, and those which are essential to the promotion of the general welfare. Within their respective territorial jurisdictions, local govemment units shall ensure and support among other things, the preservation and enrichment of culture, promote health and safety, enhance the right of the people to a balanced ecology, encourage and support the development of appropriate and self-reliant scientific and technological capabilities, improve public morals, enhance economic prosperity and social justice, promote full employment among their residents, maintain peace and order, and preserve the comfort and convenience of their inhabitants. " Accordingly, we opine that herein concemed Sangguniang Panlungsod has the authority to enact an ordinance that seeks to protect the health and well- being of its constituents. It bears stressing, however, that an ordinance enacted by virtue of the general welfare clause is valid, unless it contravenes the fundamental law of the Philippine Islands, or an Act of the Philippine Legislature, or unless it is against public policy or is unreasonable, oppressive, partial, discriminating, or in derogation of common right." In Dela Druz vs. Paraz, we laid the general rule "that ordinances passed by virtue of the implied power found in the general welfare clause must be reasonable, consonant with the general powers and purposes of the corporation and not inconsistent with the laws or policy of the State. As to the second point raised, we find that the Department is not in the best position to provide definitive guidance on whether the separation from the main office will affect the mandate and service of the other office. We defer the matter within your level to address considering that the local government unit is in the best position to act on purely local matters/concerns. As to the circumstances of separation and whether the same are compliant with the rules and regulations of the Civil Service Commission, the Commission will be in the best position to address this matter. Finally, this opinion of this Department is based solely on the facts and representations narrated from the letter and our appreciation of the same. Further, this opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts. We hope to have assisted you on this matter. Thank you very much.
